passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (MD&A) is intended to provide information that will assist the reader in understanding the company’s Consolidated Financial Statements, the changes in certain key items in those financial statements between select periods and the primary factors that accounted for those changes. In addition, we discuss how certain accounting principles, policies and critical estimates affect our Consolidated Financial Statements. Our discussion also contains certain forward-looking statements related to future events and expectations. This MD&A should be read in conjunction with our discussion of cautionary statements and significant risks to the company’s business under Item 1A. Risk Factors of the 2025 Form 10-K. Highlights for the full-year 2025 include: • Sales and revenues for 2025 were $67.589 billion, an increase of $2.780 billion, or 4 percent, compared with $64.809 billion for 2024. Sales were higher in Power & Energy , about flat in Resource Industries and slightly lower in Construction Industries . • Operating profit as a percent of sales and revenues was 16.5 percent in 2025, compared with 20.2 percent in 2024. Adjusted operating profit margin was 17.2 percent in 2025, compared with 20.7 percent in 2024. • Profit per share for 2025 was $18.81, and excluding the items in the table below, adjusted profit per share was $19.06. Profit per share for 2024 was $22.05, and excluding the items in the table below, adjusted profit per share was $21.90. • Enterprise operating cash flow was $11.7 billion in 2025. Caterpillar ended 2025 with $10.0 billion of enterprise cash. In order for our results to be more meaningful to our readers, we have separately quantified the impact of significant items. Full Year 2025 Full Year 2024 (Dollars in millions except per share data) Profit Before Taxes Profit Per Share Profit Before Taxes Profit Per Share Profit $ 11,541 $ 18.81 $ 13,373 $ 22.05 Other restructuring (income) costs 445 0.73 195 0.32 Pension/OPEB mark-to-market (gains) losses (294) (0.48) (154) (0.23) Restructuring (income) costs - divestitures of certain non-U.S. entities — — 164 0.22 Tax law change related to currency translation — — — (0.46) Adjusted profit $ 11,692 $ 19.06 $ 13,578 $ 21.90 A detailed reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures is included on pages 48 - 49. OVERVIEW Total sales and revenues for 2025 were $67.589 billion, an increase of $2.780 billion, or 4 percent, compared with $64.809 billion for 2024. The increase reflected higher sales volume , partially offset by unfavorable price realization . Higher sales volume was primarily driven by higher sales of equipment to end users. Profit per share was $18.81 in 2025, compared with profit per share of $22.05 in 2024. Profit was $8.884 billion in 2025, compared with $10.792 billion in 2024. The decrease was mainly due to unfavorable manufacturing costs and unfavorable price realization, partially offset by the profit impact of higher sales volume. Notes: • Glossary of terms included on pages 36 - 38; first occurrence of terms shown in bold italics. • Information on non-GAAP financial measures is included on pages 48 - 49. • Some amounts within this report are rounded to the millions or billions and may not add. In addition, the sum of the components reported across periods may not equal the total amount reported year-to-date due to rounding. 30 Table of Contents 2025 COMPARED WITH 2024 CONSOLIDATED SALES AND REVENUES The chart above graphically illustrates reasons for the change in consolidated sales and revenues between 2024 (at left) and 2025 (at right). Caterpillar management utilizes these charts internally to visually communicate with the company’s board of directors and employees. Total sales and revenues for 2025 were $67.589 billion, an increase of $2.780 billion, or 4 percent, compared with $64.809 billion in 2024. The increase was primarily driven by higher sales volume of $3.389 billion, partially offset by unfavorable price realization of $817 million. The increase in sales volume was mainly driven by higher sales of equipment to end users. Sales were higher in Power & Energy, about flat in Resource Industries and slightly lower in Construction Industries. North America sales increased 6 percent due to higher sales volume, partially offset by unfavorable price realization. The increase in sales volume was mainly driven by higher sales of equipment to end users. Sales increased 4 percent in Latin America primarily due to higher sales volume, partially offset by unfavorable currency impacts related to the Brazilian real. The increase in sales volume was mainly driven by higher sales of equipment to end users. EAME sales increased 4 percent mainly due to higher sales volume and favorable currency impacts related to the euro, partially offset by unfavorable price realization. The increase in sales volume was primarily driven by the impact from changes in dealer inventories. Dealer inventory increased in 2025, compared to a decrease in 2024. Asia/Pacific sales decreased 2 percent primarily due to unfavorable currency impacts related to the Australian dollar, and lower sales volume. The decrease in sales volume was mainly driven by lower sales of equipment to end users. Total dealer inventory increased about $900 million during 2025, compared to an increase of about $400 million during 2024. Machine dealer inventory decreased about $500 million during 2025, compared to a decrease of about $700 million during 2024. Dealers are independent, and the reasons for changes in their inventory levels vary, including their expectations of future demand and product delivery times. Dealers’ demand expectations take into account seasonal changes, macroeconomic conditions, machine rental rates and other factors. Delivery times can vary based on availability of product from Caterpillar factories and product distribution centers. We expect machine dealer inventory to increase in 2026 and offset the $500 million decrease in 2025. 31 Table of Contents Sales and Revenues by Segment (Millions of dollars) 2024 Sales Volum

credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure plus shareholder distributions, and free cash flow alone exceeds dividends and buybacks combined, so internal funding covers both reinvestment and returns without incremental borrowing. This supports the intermediate risk profile.

Operating margin sits above the sector median even after a year-on-year decline, reflecting pricing power in Power & Energy and the services mix. The current ratio also exceeds the sector median and improved slightly, indicating solid near-term liquidity headroom.

key_risks.text: Gross and net leverage both rose year on year and now sit above sector medians, with net leverage close to the next risk-band boundary. A modest EBITDA decline or debt increase would push the profile into a weaker tier, leaving limited cushion.

Disclosed risk factors flag tariff-driven cost pressure: operating profit margin fell sharply year on year on unfavorable manufacturing costs and price realization, and dealer inventory rose, which could reverse into destocking and weaker equipment demand.

Debt is concentrated in near-term maturities, with the next twelve months and year two together representing the bulk of scheduled repayments, while the debt figure excludes untagged current maturities. Refinancing depends on continued market access at acceptable spreads.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage remains comfortable in absolute terms but declined year on year and trails the sector median, as interest cost rose faster than operating income. Coverage still leaves substantial room above unity, so debt service is not stressed at current earnings.

Cash flow to debt and free cash flow to debt both weakened year on year and sit below sector medians, indicating comparatively slower deleveraging. Cash balances and free cash flow nonetheless cover the near-term maturity bucket, so liquidity risk appears manageable.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer retains an intermediate indicative financial risk profile, supported by scale, positive free cash flow and distributions covered internally. Leverage above sector medians and softening margins argue for a stable rather than improving trajectory; this is analyst judgement, not a rating.

Key monitorables are tariff-driven cost inflation, dealer inventory normalization and the heavy near-term maturity schedule. Continued margin erosion combined with debt-funded distributions would narrow threshold headroom; conversely, margin recovery would restore deleveraging capacity.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流穩健覆蓋資本開支加股東分派，而單靠自由現金流已超過股息與回購之和，因此內部資金足以覆蓋再投資與回報，毋須增量借貸。此支撐中等風險狀況。
即使按年下跌，營業利潤率仍高於行業中位數，反映電力與能源業務的定價能力及服務組合。流動比率亦高於行業中位數並略有改善，顯示短期流動性緩衝穩健。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿及淨槓桿均按年上升，現時高於行業中位數，淨槓桿接近下一個風險區間邊界。EBITDA輕微下降或債務增加將令狀況跌入較弱層級，緩衝有限。
披露的風險因素顯示關稅驅動的成本壓力：營業利潤率因不利的製造成本及價格實現按年大幅下降，經銷商庫存上升，可能逆轉為去庫存及設備需求轉弱。
債務集中於短期到期，未來十二個月及第二年合計佔預定還款的大部分，而債務數字不包括未標記的流動到期債務。再融資取決於能否以可接受息差持續進入市場。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率絕對水平仍穩健，但按年下降且低於行業中位數，因利息成本上升快於營業收入。覆蓋率仍遠高於一倍，故按現時盈利水平債務償付並無壓力。
現金流對債務比率及自由現金流對債務比率均按年轉弱，且低於行業中位數，顯示去槓桿相對較慢。現金結餘及自由現金流仍覆蓋短期到期債務，故流動性風險似乎可控。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人維持中等指示性財務風險狀況，受規模、正自由現金流及內部覆蓋的分派支撐。槓桿高於行業中位數及利潤率轉弱，支持穩定而非改善的軌跡；此為分析師判斷，並非評級。
主要監察事項為關稅驅動的成本通脹、經銷商庫存正常化及沉重的短期到期安排。利潤率持續侵蝕結合債務融資分派將收窄門檻緩衝；反之，利潤率復甦將恢復去槓桿能力。
